adjudication_label: Grain Structure Stability and Texture Evolution
canonical_question: If the scanning strategy is controlled to suppress <001>, will the <101> and <111> textures remain stable at the high temperatures used in the tensile tests?

question_variants.question: If the scanning strategy is controlled to suppress <001>, will the <101> and <111> textures remain stable at the high temperatures used in the tensile tests?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text mentions that controlling <001> via scanning strategy improves properties, but does not provide data on the thermal stability or stability of <101> and <111> textures specifically at the high temperatures used in tensile/compression tests.

answers.answer: The text states that strong <001> texture control with scanning strategy control will have a positive influence on mechanical properties, but it does not address whether the resulting <101> or <111> textures remain stable at the high temperatures used in the tests.
answers.conditions: High temperature tests (implied by tensile/compression context)
answers.measurement_outcome: No data on texture stability at high temperatures.
answers.boundary_limitation: Stability of <101>/<111> at high temperature is not reported.
evidence_spans: To evaluate the temperature-dependent mechanical properties of SLM-built equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, a cylindrical specimen with a size of Φ 4 mm × height 6 mm was prepared by using electrical discharge machining according to scanning direction (SD).
Compression tests were performed using MTS-810 equipment at 25, 500, 600, 700, 800, and 900 °C.
An initial strain rate of 1 × 10 −3 −1 and an engineering strain limit of 0.4 were applied.
